# Whimbrel Research data

Machine-readable data on US medtech company activity: NIH SBIR/STTR
awards, FDA 510(k) clearances, and FDA PMA approvals, read daily from
the public registries. Every event links to the public record it came
from; an event that cannot be verified against a public source is not
published. The archive behind these files currently tracks
3729 US medtech companies. The published files are a rolling window
of recent events; the archive itself is not published.

## Files

- /index.json: manifest of every file here, with schema version,
  license, and next-update time.
- /signals-latest.json: events observed in the last 14 days.
  Each event carries a stable id, company name, kind, event date,
  observed date, amount_usd where a source states a figure, a one-line
  summary, and the source URL. Updated daily.
- /stats.json: aggregate history (weekly counts and stated dollars for
  the trailing quarter) and archive scale. Aggregates only; archived
  events are not published.
- /methodology.md: how the data is collected, dated, and windowed, and
  what these files exclude.

## MCP server

The same data is queryable over the Model Context Protocol
(Streamable HTTP, no authentication) at:

https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev

Tools: latest_signals (14-day window, filterable by kind),
signal_of_the_day, weekly_pulse (computed aggregates), who_got_funded
(the window filtered by new-award freshness, phase, and amount),
micro_brief (a composed mini-dossier on any company in the archive, one company
lookup per caller per day), company_timeline (the structured version),
and about_the_data. Company records also carry patent grants, published
patent applications, and SEC funding filings.

The server also publishes one MCP prompt per tool, named with a
whimbrel_ prefix (whimbrel_micro_brief, whimbrel_latest_signals, ...), so
clients that surface prompts as slash commands get a ready-made command
palette on connect.

## The engagement behind the free tier

This data layer is the free tier. With an engagement, Whimbrel
Research does the research for you: you send companies, and you get a
full sourced brief on each, with leadership and contact routes, plus
daily monitoring for companies that match your firm's capabilities.
The first month is free. https://whimbrelresearch.com
